input.question: Why is it such a "Taboo" to talk about how much you get paid at your job with co-workers?
input.ground_truth: Companies don't want you to know what everyone else makes. It's harder to value your own worth when you only know what you make. When people know what others make, they might be more likely to demand more. So, by making sure only you know how much you make (whether through contract language or through it being "frowned upon"), the company tends to get to pay people less
